comparison: Both evaluations strongly support the findings about phospholipid binding at CDR sites (C3, C19, C27-C33). OpenEval emphasizes quantitative validation (0.6-0.7 Å RMSD, >80% occupancy), while peer reviewers highlight that simulations 'accurately and reproducibly predict ab initio binding' and 'recapitulate binding sites observed experimentally by X-ray crystallography.' Both mark as SUPPORTED with high confidence.

Perfect agreement on 10E8 findings (C39-C43). Both evaluations support the novel phosphatidylcholine binding site offset from published structures and FR-L3 involvement. OpenEval provides quantitative details (sub-Ångström stability, >500-fold reduction in neutralization), while peer reviewers note the findings are 'robust to alterations in membrane composition and rigidity.' Both mark as SUPPORTED.

Perfect agreement on FR-H3 membrane intercalation discovery (C35-C37). Both evaluations recognize this as a novel finding with implications for vaccine design. Peer reviewers describe it as 'a previously unappreciated framework region' contributing to membrane association, treating it as an important mechanistic insight. Both mark as SUPPORTED.

Both evaluations support the structural bioinformatics validation (C45-C48). OpenEval emphasizes the quantitative database search results (10^5-10^6 geometrically similar loops, only 4 and 23 phosphate-binding cases), while peer reviewers describe it as 'a comprehensive approach to validate the identified binding sites.' Both mark as SUPPORTED.

Both evaluations support LN01 findings (C57-C63), including the novel 'Loading Site' discovery. OpenEval provides quantitative occupancy data and emphasizes pre-organization mechanism, while peer reviewers note the discovery 'could guide future experiments with this antibody' and accept the conformational predisposition observations. Both mark as SUPPORTED.

Perfect agreement on CG methodology validation (C64-C72). Both evaluations emphasize the importance of negative controls (BSA, 13h11) and consistency between CG and all-atom methods. Peer reviewers note CG simulations are 'compelling because negative controls that should not associate with membrane indeed sample significantly less membrane.' Both mark as SUPPORTED.

Perfect agreement on multiscale integration approach (C73-C78). Both evaluations strongly support the CG-to-all-atom workflow. Peer reviewers explicitly state it 'provides a generalized framework for such simulations,' and OpenEval emphasizes the discriminatory power (identifying unstable conformations). Both mark as SUPPORTED.

Perfect agreement on pulling simulation validation (C80-C82). Both evaluations support the method's ability to distinguish WAWA variant with reduced membrane affinity. OpenEval emphasizes statistical significance (p<0.001, 32±13% difference), while peer reviewers note the model 'reliably predicts lower association energetics for known mutations.' Both mark as SUPPORTED.

Significant disagreement on maturation analysis (C83-C88). OpenEval marks as SUPPORTED despite noting lack of significance between Germline and Intermediate (C87), while peer reviewers mark as UNCERTAIN, explicitly noting 'the model does have limitations: namely, its ability to predict more subtle changes along a lineage.' Peer reviewers emphasize that intermediate mutations are 'indistinguishable from mutations that completely ablate lipid association.'

Perfect agreement on background/context claims (C1-C2, C8-C18). Both evaluations support these as well-established findings from prior experimental work. OpenEval notes they are 'well-supported by the cited literature,' while peer reviewers accept them as 'validated background knowledge supporting the computational investigation.' Both mark as SUPPORTED.

Both evaluations support the computational methodology (C20-C26, C89-C93). OpenEval describes them as 'factual statements about simulation setup using standard, validated approaches,' while peer reviewers affirm 'the MD simulations conducted throughout are rigorous and the analysis are extensive, creative, and biologically inspired.' Both mark as SUPPORTED.

OpenEval evaluates C34 (lipid exchange observation from single trajectory) as SUPPORTED, noting it demonstrates dynamic nature of lipid binding. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific claim.

Disagreement on differential insertion depth claim (C38). OpenEval marks as UNCERTAIN, noting the causal link to poly-specificity is speculative and requires additional validation. Peer reviewers mark as SUPPORTED, accepting the observation without critique and noting the speculative interpretation is presented cautiously. Different standards for mechanistic speculation.

Perfect agreement on MPER-TM orientation comparisons (C49-C52). Both evaluations support the quantitative comparison with experimental structures and conformational analysis. Peer reviewers treat consistency with experimental structures as validation of simulation approach. Both mark as SUPPORTED.

Disagreement on bivalent binding inference (C79). OpenEval marks as UNCERTAIN, noting it is based on structural modeling rather than simulation data and 'lacks the dynamic sampling and energetic considerations' needed for definitive conclusions. Peer reviewers mark as SUPPORTED, accepting it as a logical consequence of Fab orientation data without critique. Different standards for modeling-based inferences.
